comments.content: This pairs `isLoggedIn = true` with a `lastKnownSession` that is only as fresh as its last write (startup `primeSession()`, `getUser()`, or a sign-out), and it never checks `snapshot.isLoggedIn`. Because `isUserLoggedIn()` is `tokenFlow().map { it != null }` (no `distinctUntilChanged`), it re-emits on every token change — including a token replacement (signing in as another account via AuthenticationScreen, reachable while authenticated from RateLimitDialog). At that moment the snapshot still holds the previous account's profile, so the warm-up target is the previous account's avatar — exactly what the comment claims to prevent. The opposite failure is also reachable: after logout/session-expiry the snapshot is (false, null), so on the next `isLoggedIn = true` the URL is null and nothing re-reads the snapshot after `getUser()` records the new profile — the warm-up silently never happens for any session created after startup. Re-prime under the current token before reading (primeSession()'s ownedCachedProfile stamp check makes it token-safe) and gate on the snapshot's own flag. (For warm-up to actually work after an in-app login, the URL would ultimately need to come from getUser()'s emission, since the post-login cache is empty.)

This introduces a direct Kermit dependency in the ViewModel, bypassing the project's logging seam (`KomiStoreLogger`, injected into repositories such as UserSessionRepositoryImpl). Using the same abstraction keeps log routing/behavior consistent across targets and keeps the ViewModel testable with a fake logger.

comments.content: `avatarSizePx` depends on `LocalDensity`, which can change at runtime on desktop (window moved to a monitor with a different DPI, or an OS scale-factor change), but it is not a LaunchedEffect key — the effect captures whatever value was current when the URL last changed. A warm-up that runs after a density change then decodes at the stale pixel size, misses the size-keyed memory-cache entry the profile card will request (whose avatar runs with `showLoadingIndicator = false`), and the avatar shows a brief empty frame — one of the flashes this PR is meant to remove. Add the size to the keys so the prefetch re-runs at the new density.

comments.content: The `80.dp` here silently duplicates `Modifier.size(80.dp)` of the avatar in `SignedInContent` (ProfileSections.kt, core/feature presentation). The warm-up only hits the memory cache when the decoded size exactly matches the size the profile card resolves (Coil includes the resolved size in the memory-cache key), so if the card's avatar size ever changes, the warm-up degrades to a disk-cache decode with a visible flash and no compile error. Extract a shared constant (e.g. `val ProfileAvatarSize = 80.dp` in core:presentation next to GitHubStoreImage) and use it in both places.

comments.content: The ownership guard silently disables exactly where it's needed. `ownershipStamp()` returns null for any token that never went through `DefaultTokenStore.save()` — notably legacy tokens stored by `migrateIfNeeded()`, which `safePut`s the parsed token without stamping (`isTokenExpired()` also defends against a null stamp, confirming unstamped tokens exist in the wild). With `current == null` this check passes unconditionally, so after a token rotation (sign-in via PAT/web-auth just overwrites the token; nothing in the login flow clears the profile cache) account B is primed from account A's cached profile via the `get`/`getStale` fallback below. The stated compat goal only requires accepting caches whose *stored* stamp is null (written before this field existed); it does not require accepting a known owner's cache for an unstamped token. Dropping the `current != null` conjunct keeps pre-stamp caches readable while closing the hole.

comments.content: Stamp lifecycle desync on the fetch path: when `ownershipStamp(token)` is null (legacy/unstamped token), this `?.let` silently skips the write, so `CACHE_KEY` now holds the *new* account's profile while `CACHE_OWNER_KEY` keeps the *previous* owner's stamp. A later read for the previous owner (e.g. a restored token with the same saved-at value) then passes the stamp check and is served the wrong account's profile. Write the stamp unconditionally — or, when it is unknown, clear the owner key so the pair degrades to "owner unknown" instead of "owned by someone else". Also consider putting the owner stamp before the profile so a crash between the two writes degrades to a rejected cache rather than a misattributed one.

comments.content: Emission and snapshot disagree: this branch emits `null` ("no user") but leaves `_lastKnownSession` untouched, so it can still report `(isLoggedIn = true, oldProfile)`. The comment claims "do not flip the session back to logged-in" — but nothing records the signed-out state either, despite the interface contract that `clearLastKnownSession` is called "wherever the token is found to be gone". The two sign-out paths (`logout()`, 401) already record `(false, null)`, so the reachable gap is token *rotation* (another account signs in via `AuthenticationRepositoryImpl`, which never records a snapshot): the stale old account then seeds the next first frame — `ProfileViewModel` builds its initial `ProfileState` and `MainViewModel` reads `lastKnownSession?.profile?.imageUrl` as the avatar warm-up target, rendering/warming the previous account. Record an honest snapshot in the else branch: signed-out if the store is now empty, `(true, null)` ("token valid, account not read yet") if a different account rotated in. Same fix needed at the fetch-success else branch (~line 156) and the stale-fallback else branch (~line 172).

comments.content: A transient failure with an unreadable/evicted cache unconditionally downgrades the snapshot from a known `(true, profile)` to `(true, null)`. Consumers interpret `(true, null)` as "account not read yet": `ProfileViewModel` seeds `isUserLoggedIn = session.isLoggedIn && session.profile != null` -> false, so the next first frame flashes the signed-out "Sign in" card for a logged-in user — the exact rebuild flash this PR fixes. Reachable via `CacheRepositoryImpl.clearAll()` (user's clear-cache action), hourly `cleanupExpired()` after the 6h TTL, or a corrupt row deleted by `CacheManager.get`'s decode fallback, combined with a failed refetch. Preserve the previously recorded profile on failure instead of wiping it. Trade-off: in the rare in-process account-rotation window this keeps the old account's profile a little longer; if strictness there matters more, stamp the snapshot with `ownershipStamp(token)` and only preserve on match.

comments.content: Check-then-act race: `isCurrentToken()` -> `recordSession()` -> `emit()` is not atomic. A `logout()` completing between the check and the record rewrites `_lastKnownSession` to `(true, oldProfile)` *after* `logout()` recorded `(false, null)`, so the snapshot reports a signed-in session for a logged-out user until the next read corrects it — and a screen constructed in that window seeds the old account. (Small, self-healing window, hence low.) While fixing it, the identical 5-line gate is repeated at all four emission sites (cache-hit, fetch-success, stale-fallback, no-stale-fallback); collapsing it into one helper keeps the snapshot/emit contract in a single place and centralizes the else-branch fix above.

comments.content: Platform-specific annotation in common code: `@Volatile` resolves to `kotlin.jvm.Volatile` (no explicit `kotlin.jvm`/`kotlin.concurrent` import, matching the existing convention in e.g. `ProxyManager`/`GitHubClientProvider`). Both current targets (Android, desktop) are JVM so it works today, but as a JVM `@OptionalExpectation` it silently becomes a no-op on any future native target, leaving `_lastKnownSession` (written on `Dispatchers.IO`, read from the UI thread) without a visibility guarantee — exactly the class of platform leak the review asks about. Import `kotlin.concurrent.Volatile` (the multiplatform common annotation) for portable semantics.

comments.content: Contract overpromise: "Never null after the first read" is not enforced by the implementation. `primeSession()` is fallible (its only caller, `MainViewModel`, catches and continues on failure) and `getUser()` may never run in a session, so `lastKnownSession` can legitimately stay null past the first read. Consumers currently use safe calls (`?.profile?.imageUrl`), but this doc invites `!!`-style assumptions. Either reword the contract to "null until the first successful observation" or make the impl guarantee non-null (e.g. `primeSession()` recording a `(false, null)` snapshot even on partial failure).

comments.content: Setting isUserLoggedIn = true before any profile emission re-creates exactly the (isUserLoggedIn = true, userProfile = null) combination the seed above masks. HeroIdentityCard decides the card by userProfile alone (ProfileSections.kt:216), so this flag cannot keep the signed-out card out of "the gap" as the comment claims — it only adds the Stars/Logout rows around it. The result is the "Sign in" card above the stars/logout rows for the entire loadUserProfile() fetch (a network round-trip when the cache misses, not "a frame"), and indefinitely when getUser() emits null (fetch failure with no cache — UserSessionRepositoryImpl records (true, null) and emits null). Keep the seed's invariant: don't set the flag here; set it in loadUserProfile's update as it.copy(userProfile = profile, isUserLoggedIn = profile != null), or gate the library/account rows on userProfile != null (see the ProfileSections comment).

There is only one implementation (`DefaultTokenStore`), which I already read. `tokenFlow()` = `flow { migrationDeferred.await(); emitAll(ksafe.safeGetFlow<GithubDeviceTokenSuccessDto?>(tokenKey, null)) }`.

`safeGetFlow`: 
- If `getFlow(key, default)` throws at build time → `flow { emit(defaultValue) }` → emits `null` once and completes.
- Otherwise `upstream.catch { ... emit(defaultValue) }` — on a mid-stream error, emits `null` (and completes since catch's emit is terminal).

So `isUserLoggedIn()` can emit a spurious one-shot `false` when KSafe's flow build fails or its stream errors. The codebase explicitly plans for transient KSafe failures (the whole KSafeSafe wrapper). Also what does `KSafe.getFlow` do — StateFlow-backed? Whatever it is, the error paths are real per the wrapper.

Additionally — one more subtle case: `safeGetFlow`'s fallback `flow { emit(defaultValue) }` completes → `isUserLoggedIn()`'s collect in the VM ends permanently → given `hasLoadedInitialData = true`, `observeLoggedInStatus` never restarts → stuck. The stuck part is pre-existing, but the new `clearLastKnownSession()` makes the transient failure destroy the process-wide snapshot.

Hmm — one more thought on issue #3's framing. Per the repository's own contract doc: clearLastKnownSession "Called wherever the token is found to be gone". Is a `false` emission from `isUserLoggedIn()` "the token is found to be gone"? By the flow's definition yes. But the *source* of the emission might be the error fallback (not a real absence). The repository layer knows the difference (safeGetFlow logs "build failed; emitting default"); the VM doesn't. So the clear belongs at the repository layer where the fallback happens — e.g., `UserSessionRepositoryImpl` should record the signed-out snapshot when it observes the token vanish (it already does in logout/notifySessionExpired; the remaining "token disappeared without a logout" gap is `tokenStore.clear()` called elsewhere or `safeDelete` failures). Replacing the token (new login) doesn't clear. `safePut` failing? That keeps the old token. `safeGet`/`getFlow` transient failure → returns default → *appears* gone without being gone — exactly the false-positive case! So ironically, the only realistic way "the token disappears without a logout" is the transient-failure false positive — in which case clearing the snapshot is precisely wrong. comments.content: Behavior regression: `ownedCachedProfile()` falls back to `getStale()`, which returns *expired* rows (`CacheDao.getAny`). Before this change the hot read was fresh-only (`cacheManager.get`), so an expired entry made `getUser()` fall through to the network and refresh the cache. Now an expired-but-not-yet-erased row is treated as a "cache hit" and `return@flow` below skips the fetch entirely — `cleanupExpired()` runs at most hourly, so for that whole window the profile is served stale with no refresh attempt even when online. It also contradicts `primeSession()`'s comment "the normal read replaces it moments later": the normal read accepts the same stale row and never replaces it with fresh data. Fix: give `ownedCachedProfile` an `allowStale` flag (e.g. `return cacheManager.get(CACHE_KEY) ?: if (allowStale) cacheManager.getStale(CACHE_KEY) else null`), use fresh-only here, and pass `allowStale = true` only in `primeSession()` and the error fallback.

comments.content: `ImageLoader.enqueue` is fire-and-forget, so it escapes the `LaunchedEffect`'s lifecycle: when `signedInAvatarUrl` changes (sign-out, 401 expiry, account switch) the effect is cancelled/restarted but the already-dispatched request keeps running and writes the previous account's avatar into the shared Coil caches — exactly the cross-account warm-up the MainViewModel comments try to prevent. Also, `runCatching` around `enqueue` only guards the synchronous request build; the actual fetch/decode failure arrives in the async callback and is silently dropped (the `Result` here is discarded), so this error handling is illusory. Use the suspending `execute` so the fetch participates in structured concurrency and is aborted when the key changes or the user signs out (and remember to rethrow `CancellationException` if you wrap it in try/catch).
